lines: A blank panel in the maker's purple whose width you set yourself
Note — drag either edge of the panel to make it wider or narrower; it will not go below 6HP.
Note — the width is saved with the patch.
Three chaotic oscillators run from one set of controls at three different speeds, with their outputs and a weighted average of them
Sets how fast all three systems travel along their orbits; each runs at its own fraction of the setting, so they drift apart at different rates
Adjusts a constant in all three systems at once, 0.1 to 10, each system mapping that onto its own usable span
Sets the voltage the outputs span, from about ±0.1V at the bottom of its travel through ±5V at the centre to about ±10V fully clockwise
Adds to the speed knob, a fifth of a unit per volt
Adds to the shape knob, two units per volt
Adds to the scale knob, two units per volt
The x coordinate of the Halvorsen attractor, the fastest of the three
The y coordinate of the Halvorsen attractor, the fastest of the three
The z coordinate of the Halvorsen attractor, the fastest of the three
x plus y minus z from the Halvorsen attractor, the maker's own fourth output
The x coordinate of the Dadras attractor, which runs at two thirds the speed of the Halvorsen one
The y coordinate of the Dadras attractor, which runs at two thirds the speed of the Halvorsen one
The z coordinate of the Dadras attractor, which runs at two thirds the speed of the Halvorsen one
x plus y minus z from the Dadras attractor, the maker's own fourth output
The x coordinate of the Lorenz attractor, which runs far slower than the other two
The y coordinate of the Lorenz attractor, which runs far slower than the other two
The z coordinate of the Lorenz attractor, which runs far slower than the other two
x plus y minus z from the Lorenz attractor, the maker's own fourth output
A weighted average of the three systems' x outputs, with the Dadras one carrying most of the weight
A weighted average of the three systems' y outputs, with the Dadras one carrying most of the weight
A weighted average of the three systems' z outputs, with the Dadras one carrying most of the weight
A weighted average of the three systems' fourth outputs, with the Dadras one carrying most of the weight
Note — the three systems are only calculated while a cable is patched to one of the sixteen outputs.
Note — a chaotic system is not held inside the range the scale knob sets, and the outputs will now and then go above or below it.
Note — a value that escapes to infinity is caught and set back to zero, so the module recovers on its own.

languor.notes: The three systems share the speed knob through fixed multipliers: halvorsen 0.75, dadras 0.5 and lorenz 0.03 (languor.cpp:99, 114, 129), so the lorenz column moves about twenty-five times slower than the halvorsen one. The shape knob is mapped separately onto each system's own usable span (languor.cpp:98, 113, 128).

lines: Chaotic low-frequency oscillator running the Halvorsen attractor, a set of equations whose orbit never repeats, giving four wandering voltages
Sets how fast the system travels along its orbit, from a thousandth of full rate at the bottom of its travel to full rate at the top
Adjusts one constant in the equations, 1.23 to 1.63, which changes the shape of the orbit; below that the system runs away and above it it stops being chaotic
Sets the voltage the four outputs span, from about ±0.1V at the bottom of its travel through ±5V at the centre to about ±10V fully clockwise
The x coordinate of the system, scaled to the range set by the scale knob
The y coordinate of the system, scaled to the range set by the scale knob
The z coordinate of the system, scaled to the range set by the scale knob
x plus y minus z, the maker's own fourth output, scaled to the range set by the scale knob
Note — the system is only calculated while a cable is patched to one of the four outputs.
Note — a chaotic system is not held inside the range the scale knob sets, and the outputs will now and then go above or below it; put a clamp or a limiter after them where that matters.

lines: A large oscilloscope that plots two signals against time or against each other, on a black panel you can widen to any size
The first signal to plot; in Lissajous mode it is the horizontal axis, and in waveform mode it is drawn against time and is also the trigger
The second signal to plot; in Lissajous mode it is the vertical axis, and in waveform mode it is drawn against time
Sets the colour the trace is drawn in, 0-6V taking it once round the hue circle; with nothing patched the trace is drawn in the maker's orange
Adds to the rotation knob, one unit per volt
Lengthens the stretch of time the picture covers, doubling it for each volt
Shifts the first signal before it is drawn, -10V to 10V added to it
Shifts the second signal before it is drawn, -10V to 10V added to it
Sets how far the first signal is magnified, in steps of a power of two from a quarter up to 256 times
Sets how far the second signal is magnified, in steps of a power of two from a quarter up to 256 times
Sets how fast the picture spins, -10 to 10
Sets how long a stretch of signal the picture covers, 4 to 16, each step up halving it
Menu — Lissajous mode — plots the first signal against the second instead of plotting both against time
Menu — Show statistics — prints the highest and lowest voltage held in each buffer above the picture
Note — drag either edge of the panel to make it wider or narrower; it will not go below 13HP.
Note — in waveform mode the first signal is also the trigger: the drawing restarts when it rises past 1V, or after a tenth of a second if it does not.

fullscope.notes: The enum lists TIME_INPUT before ROTATION_INPUT but the widget adds the rotation jack first (fullscope.cpp:328-329), so down the panel strip the fourth hole is input 4 and the fifth is input 3; tagging from the enum order would have swapped the two lines. LISSAJOUS_PARAM, TRIG_PARAM and EXTERNAL_PARAM are declared but never configured and have no widget, so parameters 5, 6 and 7 cannot be reached; the trigger threshold line that would have used TRIG_PARAM is commented out (fullscope.cpp:122). The x and y jacks are left without a family because a scope carries whatever is patched to it.
